sentences.text:
Amit Kumar Jadiya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10
January, 2025
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Jbp:1244
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

At Jabalpur
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Devnarayan Mishra
 On The 10th Of January, 2025
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 55954 of 2024
 Amit Kumar Jadiya
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:
 Mr. Mukesh Kumar Pandey - Advocate for applicant.
Mr. Vinod Mishra - Panel Lawyer for State.
Mr. Anand Jha - Advocate for complainant.

Order 
This is the first application filed by the applicant under Section 482 of Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita , 2023/Section 438 of Cr.P.C., 1973 seeking anticipatory bail in connection with Crime No.530 of 2024 for offences punishable under Sections 376 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code registered at Police Station-Kamla Nagar, District-Bhopal (M.P.).
2.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant and the victim are the residents of Panna.

With the consent, the victim left her parental home and went along with the applicant to Bhopal where they performed the marriage on 24.03.2023 in Arya Samaj Kendra, Nehru Nagar,
Bhopal.
On 04.04.2024, marriage was registered before the Marriage Registrar Municipal Corporation, Bhopal.

Both were residing as husband and wife and after occurring the dispute between the parties, the applicant filed NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:1244 2 MCRC-55954-2024 application under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act for restitution of conjugal rights on 25.09.2024 before the Family Court, Panna and the victim/wife filed a petition for divorce before the Family Court, Sagar that was registered as RCSHM 181 of 2024 on 28.07.2024 and thus, it is clear that both were residing together as husband and wife.
After all these proceedings, family members of the wife/victim by making pressure on victim to lodge F.I.R..
A false F.I.R. was registered on 30.10.2024 at Police Station-Kamla Nagar Bhopal suppressing the fact of the marriage.
He has submitted that the matter can be sought out by a mutual settlement.

Hence,
he be enlarged on bail.

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the objector has submitted that anticipatory bail should not be entertained as it will effect the investigation.

4. Learned Government Advocate for the State has submitted that on verification, it was found that a divorce petition and a petition for restitution of conjugal rights are pending before the Family Court but has objected that the marriage was performed forcibly.
Hence, the applicant may not be granted the benefit of anticipatory bail.

5. Heard the parties and perused the record.
6.

Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case coupled with the fact that marriage was performed on 24.03.2023 and divorce petition filed by the victim on 28.07.2024, till then no F.I.R.
and allegations were levelled that the marriage was performed with undue pressure or applying the threat or influencing in any other manner, this Court deems it appropriate to enlarge the applicant on anticipatory bail, therefore, without commenting on the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:1244 3 MCRC-55954-2024 merit of the case, the application is allowed.
7.

It is directed that in the event of arrest the applicant shall be enlarged on bail on furnishing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) each with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer for applicant appearance before him during the course of investigation or before the trial Court concerned during trial, as the case may be.
8. It is further directed that the applicant shall abide by all the conditions as enumerated under Section 482(2) of BNSS.
9. Applicant shall cooperate in the investigation and if required samples of blood shall also be taken.
10. Accordingly, M.Cr.C. stands disposed of.
11. C.C. as per rules.

(DEVNARAYAN MISHRA) JUDGE julie Amit Kumar Jadiya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3786581/
